section_summaries.group_design: retrospective cohort study of patients identified from Mayo Clinic anti-GAD65 samples submitted between 2003 and 2018 study of 212 patients with GAD65 neurological autoimmunity evaluation of a large patient cohort with high-titre GAD65 antibodies systematically determined to have GAD65 neurological autoimmunity
section_summaries.group_characteristics: 323 patients with high-titre (>20 nmol/L in serum) GAD65 antibodies identified from 380,514 submitted samples; after chart review, 108 patients were classified as not having GAD65 neurological autoimmunity and 3 had atypical presentations 212 patients; median age at symptom onset 46 years (range 5–83); 77% female; SPSD (N=71), cerebellar ataxia (N=55), epilepsy (N=35), limbic encephalitis (N=7), overlap syndrome (N=44); cognitive impairment (N=38), myelopathy (N=23), brainstem dysfunction (N=22) 323 patients with high-titre GAD65 antibodies identified from 380,514 samples submitted for anti-GAD65 testing
section_summaries.group_findings: SPSD, cerebellar ataxia, epilepsy, and limbic encephalitis designated core manifestations; cognitive impairment, myelopathy, and brainstem dysfunction designated secondary manifestations; cerebellar ataxia and serum GAD65 antibody titre >500 nmol/L predicted poor outcome Patients with non-neurological presentations or more likely alternative diagnoses were excluded from study analysis and summarized separately Electroencephalography for epilepsy was frequently gathered, but an abnormal electrophysiological study was not required for diagnosis given imperfect test clinical specificity
section_summaries.group_treatment_outcomes: Sustained response to immunotherapy ranged from 5/20 (25%) in epilepsy to 32/44 (73%) in SPSD (p=0.002); complete immunotherapy response occurred in 2/142 (1%) Response to immunotherapy (corticosteroids, intravenous IG, plasma exchange, rituximab, cyclophosphamide and/or autologous stem cell transplantation) was classified as no response, partial response, near-complete response, or complete response, as well as sustained (benefit persisting >3 months) or non-sustained, based on review of treating physician’s documentation Eight of 62 patients (13%) underwent epilepsy surgery (unilateral anterior temporal lobectomy, 7 patients; unilateral anterolateral temporal/frontal lobe resections, 1 patient)
section_summaries.group_limitations: None explicitly stated Previous reports are limited by small sample sizes or restriction to individual phenotypes, precluding complete disease characterisation Patients with non-neurological presentations or alternative diagnoses were excluded, potentially limiting generalizability
